clue.text: Tourist takes farmworker around strange lido

indicators.note: the farmworker's letters go around the jumbled lido, holding it inside

parts.note: a haymaker is a farm labourer who cuts and turns grass for fodder

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of lido are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor brings a farm labourer along to a peculiar open-air swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns LIDO into OLID, which 'around' puts inside HAYMAKER after its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on vacation travelling for pleasure is a tourist.

clue.text: Straightness of plant…

definitions.meaning: straightness here is moral uprightness, truthful dealing
a garden flower with papery silver seed pods, also called lunaria

explanation.surface: A botanical note on how upright a certain plant grows, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour and straight dealing are virtues of an upright person; the plant lunaria shares the name.

clue.text: … cattle-fodder from the lake

definitions.meaning: a clover-like crop, alfalfa, grown to feed livestock
a large Swiss lake beside the city of the same name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a plant used to feed cattle, taken from a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa grown as fodder has this British name, and a famous Swiss lake shares it.

clue.text: French ground in hollow is a hindrance

indicators.note: in places the French word inside the hollow's letters

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface
terre is the French word for earth or ground

explanation.surface: French soil lying in a depression proves an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets TERRE inside DENT, between DE and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that puts people off acting is an obstacle or check.

clue.text: Fresh litter?

definitions.meaning: fresh in the sense of new, not yet old
a litter of puppies or kittens is an animal's brood of offspring

explanation.surface: A question about whether newly dropped rubbish counts as fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish, but here it is a brood of newborn animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenile means fresh and youthful, and a mother animal's babies are collectively called this.

clue.text: Copper in new case takes a day to be charged

indicators.note: in puts the copper symbol inside the reworked case
new signals the letters of case are made over in a fresh order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman on a fresh case spends a day before someone is formally charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CASE into ACSE; 'in' sets CU inside it to make ACCUSE, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A person charged with a crime stands formally indicted in court.

clue.text: Write Far From The Madding Crowd, for example?

definitions.text: Write Far From The Madding Crowd, for example?

parts.words: Write Far From The Madding Crowd, for example?
parts.note: the phrase is a line from Gray's mournful poem in a country churchyard, so writing it means composing a lament

explanation.surface: An instruction to write Hardy's novel about Bathsheba Everdene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Thomas Hardy's novel, but Hardy took his title from Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, so writing it is composing an elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose a mournful poem for the dead is to write an elegy.

clue.text: Blame lingers, having shifted these sculptures

indicators.note: having shifted signals that the letters of the two words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Blame for their removal still hangs around these statues once they were moved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to the lasting row over Lord Elgin's removal of the Parthenon sculptures to London.
explanation.definitionFit: The marble friezes from the Parthenon in Athens, now in the British Museum, are famous sculptures.

clue.text: Liberal leaders count out this relief work

parts.note: the leading letters of Liberal, its first two

indicators.note: out here means the letters of count are put out of order

explanation.surface: Senior Liberal figures exclude this charitable relief project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' suggests aid work; here it is a print made from a block carved in relief. 'out' turns COUNT into NOCUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A print taken from a design carved into a linoleum block is a kind of relief print.

clue.text: Pawnbroker carrying article that is stained

indicators.note: carrying here means bearing the article along behind it

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker carries a soiled item.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stained is dirty or soiled, not clean.

clue.text: Late shifts, possibly

parts.note: shifts read as garments, nightdresses worn late in the evening, not stints of work

explanation.surface: A note on working the late shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A shift is also a loose dress, and a late one is worn at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightdresses worn in bed are garments for the night.

clue.text: One will receive many forms of proposal at work

definitions.text: One will receive many forms of proposal at work

parts.words: One will receive many forms of proposal at work
parts.note: proposal forms are what one fills in to apply for a policy, so a firm offering cover receives many of them

explanation.surface: Someone at the office who gets lots of marriage offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposal' suggests marriage, but a proposal form is an application for insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that underwrites policies receives applications called proposal forms.

clue.text: Cooking-assembly for discussion group?

parts.note: gas is informal for idle talk or chatter
a ring is a group or circle of people

explanation.surface: Is a cooker part fit for a discussion group?
explanation.definitionFit: A burner on a hob fuelled by mains supply is a cooking unit.

clue.text: Live on hawthorn? Possibly!

indicators.note: on here means the live word is placed after the hawthorn word

parts.note: may is another name for hawthorn blossom
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Could one survive on hawthorn? Perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps expresses that something could happen.

clue.text: Means suitable to an end manoeuvre

definitions.meaning: a means of reaching a goal, convenient rather than principled
a manoeuvre in the sense of a stratagem or shift

explanation.surface: A tactical move that serves its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A convenient device or ploy used to get something done is a stratagem.

clue.text: Frost in safe confines

indicators.note: in places the frost word inside the safe word

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Ice forms within a strongbox's walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets RIME inside PETER, after PE.
explanation.definitionFit: The confines of an area are its boundary line.

clue.text: Controller of regal tour to be appointed

indicators.note: to be appointed suggests the letters are to be arranged afresh, set in new order

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a royal tour about to be named.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or official that governs a process is a controller.

clue.text: Badminton, for example, to contain dangerous leap of horses

indicators.note: to contain means the game word holds the dangerous word within

parts.note: badminton is an example of a game
bad can mean dangerous, as in a bad bend

explanation.surface: Badminton horse trials include a risky jump by horses.
explanation.walkthrough: BADMINTON is also a famous English horse trials event, which makes the surface equestrian. 'to contain' puts BAD inside GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A curvet or bound made by a horse is a kind of equine leap.

clue.text: On-side stroke, a practical joke?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a shot hit to the leg (on) side of the field
a hoax or tease played on someone

explanation.surface: A cricket shot that turns out to be a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, also called the on side, is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tease or hoax that fools someone is a wind-up, and a cricket shot to the leg side shares the name.

clue.text: Gross slug with a long tail

indicators.note: with means the following letters are attached to the drink

parts.note: a slug of spirits is a tot, a small drink

explanation.surface: A huge garden slug with a long tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slug' suggests the garden pest; it is a small measure of liquor. 'tail' says A and L follow on as a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A gross sum is the whole amount before deductions.

clue.text: Strain of rattling one's tin

indicators.note: rattling shakes up the letters of the words, jumbling their order

explanation.surface: The stress of shaking one's collecting tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress or tautness is strain.

clue.text: Wrong on river to cause pain?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the wrong is placed above the river

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Doing harm beside a river to hurt someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment or inflict suffering is to cause pain.

clue.text: Common cat lies outside French porcelain centre

indicators.note: outside means the letters of lies wrap round the cat word

parts.note: mog is a common, informal British word for a cat

explanation.surface: An ordinary cat sprawls outdoors in a French china town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts LIES around MOG, splitting it LI...ES. MOG is everyday British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in central France famed for its fine china is a porcelain centre.

clue.text: Made notes about long informal items in delivery

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes around the long abbreviation

parts.note: to make musical notes is to sing, past tense sang

explanation.surface: Singers going on at length about casual pieces of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' means the way one speaks, so the items are colloquial words.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial words and phrases used in casual speech make up informal vocabulary.

clue.text: Change of raiment for the eastern tower

indicators.note: change of means the letters of raiment are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A change of clothes for the oriental tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender tower of a mosque, typical of the Islamic East, is this tower.

clue.text: Bone cup, alas, is broken

indicators.note: is broken means the letters of the words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A cup has broken, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder blade is a bone of the body.

clue.text: Throne for a champion

definitions.meaning: a raised platform or a bishop's seat in an apse
a defender of popular rights, like the Roman officer protecting plebeians

explanation.surface: A seat of power awarded to a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman people's officer defended the commons, and the word also names a raised dais or bishop's seat.

clue.text: EEC green bill excited hostility

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of the three words are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A European Community environmental bill provoked aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive, warlike attitude is hostility.
